narrative:
The model estimates an 85% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns in your profile that strongly align with employees who tend to depart.

The three factors that most influenced this prediction were your overall years of experience, whether you received other job offers while working here, and how long you have been with this specific organization. 

Your total professional experience of 6-10 years was the strongest driver pushing the prediction toward leaving. Among employees the model expects to stay, half have only 1-5 years of total experience, so your mid-range tenure signals higher mobility risk. Similarly, having received other job opportunities during your time here was the second-biggest factor increasing the likelihood of departure; most employees predicted to stay never received such offers. Finally, your 1-5 years in this current role also contributed to the “will leave” direction, as shorter tenure at one employer often correlates with higher turnover in the data.

Taken together, these three elements created a clear picture of someone who is experienced enough to be attractive to other employers and already has options available.

The organization should discuss retention strategies with you, such as clearer promotion paths, better compensation alignment, or additional development support. You may also want to reflect on whether your current role still matches your longer-term goals. Addressing these areas could change the outlook for both sides. (248 words)
